app_documentation:
RetailSync Real-Time Inventory Manager is a mobile-first Progressive Web App (PWA) for small and mid-size retail stores. It gives staff a live, accurate view of stock on the shop floor. It runs in a browser on phones, tablets and desktops (screens 360px wide and up). The front end is built with React, the back end with Node.js and a REST API, and data is stored in PostgreSQL. Live updates are pushed to every connected device over WebSockets. The main purpose is to replace manual stock counting and spreadsheets with fast barcode-driven updates, real-time stock counts, proactive low-stock alerts and simple reporting.

The MVP has five features. F1 Barcode Scanning (High priority) lets clerks scan products with the device camera (ZXing) or a USB/Bluetooth handheld scanner. A scan shows product details and stock within 1 second, and unknown barcodes offer to create a new product. A Receive Delivery batch mode adds delivered stock quickly. F2 Real-Time Stock Tracking (High) keeps quantities in sync across all devices within 2 seconds. Manual adjustments require a reason code (Damaged, Lost, Received, Sold, Correction) and are written to an append-only audit ledger with user, timestamp and reason. F3 Low-Stock Alerts and Reordering (Medium) lets managers set per-product reorder thresholds. It sends an alert when quantity drops below the threshold and generates draft purchase orders grouped by the assigned supplier. F4 Inventory Reports and Dashboard (Medium) shows stock value, low-stock and out-of-stock counts, top sellers, turnover and movement history, with CSV export of a chosen date range within 10 seconds. F5 User and Role Management (Low) lets owners create staff accounts, assign roles and deactivate users. Deactivated users cannot log in, and the failed attempts are logged.

The intended users are three roles. Store Owners get dashboards, reports and team administration. Store Managers handle alerts, thresholds and purchase orders. Store Clerks scan items, receive deliveries and adjust stock. Role-based access control is enforced on every API endpoint, and clerks see an access-denied state on admin screens. The UI uses role-aware bottom navigation (Dashboard, Scan, Alerts, Reports, Team), an Inter-based design system, WCAG AA contrast, 48px touch targets and screen-reader announcements for live stock changes.

Key non-functional targets: stock updates and barcode lookups complete within 2 and 1 seconds respectively at 50 concurrent users; all traffic uses TLS 1.2+ and passwords are hashed with bcrypt; availability is 99.5% monthly uptime with daily automated backups and a 24-hour recovery point objective; and a new clerk can be trained in under 15 minutes. The database has 20 tables, including products, product_barcodes, inventory_levels (with optimistic locking), stock_movements, low_stock_alerts, purchase_orders and users/roles/permissions. The plan is 15 tasks (T1-T15) covering schema, API and auth, UI, real-time sync, alerts, reports and final load and acceptance testing. Known risks are camera scanning reliability, Wi-Fi-dependent real-time sync, no offline support in the MVP, large scope for a small team and RBAC coverage gaps. Support should be aware of these when triaging issues.

Glossary_v1 (controlled definitions of key RetailSync terms)

glossary.PWA (Progressive Web App): A web application that installs and runs like a native mobile app from the browser. RetailSync uses it so staff can use phones, tablets or desktops without an app store.
glossary.Reorder Threshold: The per-product stock quantity below which a low-stock alert is triggered for managers. It is stored in products.reorder_threshold and also guides draft purchase orders.
glossary.Stock Movement: An immutable ledger entry recording every stock change (sale, receipt, adjustment or return). It stores the signed quantity change, user, timestamp, reason and cost/price snapshots, and is the source for audit history, reports and CSV exports.
glossary.Reason Code: A required label for manual stock adjustments (for example Damaged, Lost, Received, Sold or Correction). It explains why quantity changed and is logged with the user and timestamp.
glossary.RBAC (Role-Based Access Control): The security model in which Store Owner, Store Manager and Store Clerk roles map to permissions enforced on every API endpoint. For example, clerks are denied access to admin settings and the Team screen.
glossary.Draft Purchase Order: A not-yet-submitted order to a supplier, generated from selected low-stock items and grouped by the product's preferred supplier. Managers can edit quantities before saving it.
